standard_prerequisites.name: The Shore-blocking functional and its twisting
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma_k is the functional constructed by the Shore-blocking lemma, and it can be twisted so that convergence at an index forces convergence at every smaller index and the values form a strictly decreasing sequence of ordinals below the natural product of beta with k; retained at source lines 426-431 and used in the first lines of the proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the functional that the counted lemma forces to be partial, and the twisting is what makes the ordinal rank below strictly decrease.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nodes, trees, universality and satisfaction in the SEM forcing
standard_prerequisites.statement: A node is an M-finite sequence of pairs of a bit and an M-finite transitive subset of X_a, with the set pi of the node being their union with sigma; a tree is a downward closed set of nodes and it is universal when every non-leaf can be extended on one of the two sides of every sufficiently long finite partition; a tree satisfies a formula when all its nodes do; retained at source lines 819-829 and 853-861.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the objects of the two cases of the proof, and the definition of pi is what the ordinal rank is computed on.

standard_prerequisites.name: Maximal enumerations and the finite-tree forcing lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: For every Sigma^0_1 formula and every condition there is a monotone enumeration of a maximal universal tree satisfying it, and if such a tree is M-finite then an extension forces the formula at some index and its negation at the next; retained at source lines 863-865 and 893-897.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof applies the first to the formula that says the functional converges, and the second in the case where the resulting tree is M-finite.

standard_prerequisites.name: Ordinal rank of a finite tree and well-foundedness of a supremum
standard_prerequisites.statement: To a finite tree one assigns the ordinal obtained by summing over its nodes, replacing each leaf by omega raised to the value of the functional at that leaf and each internal node by the natural sum of its successors; the hypothesis WF of the supremum of omega to the natural product with omega below alpha forbids an M-infinite decreasing sequence of such ordinals.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof defines exactly this rank zeta_s for the stages of the enumeration and shows that it strictly decreases while staying below omega to the natural product of beta with omega, contradicting the hypothesis.

core_obligations: Twist the functional so that convergence at an index implies convergence at every smaller index and the values are a strictly decreasing sequence of ordinals below the natural product of beta with k (source lines 937-941).

Form the Sigma^0_1(Y) formula saying that the functional converges at the given index, and apply the maximal-enumeration lemma to obtain a monotone enumeration of a maximal universal tree E satisfying it; split into the two cases according to whether E is M-finite (source lines 944-945).

First case: if E is M-finite then the finite-tree forcing lemma gives an extension and an index q such that the extension forces the formula at q minus one and its negation at q, which in particular forces the functional to diverge (source line 947).

Second case: assume E is not M-finite, so M-infinitely many stages change it, and speed the enumeration up so that every stage grows and no stage is the bare root; define for every stage s and node nu of E[s] the ordinal rank zeta_s(nu), equal to omega raised to the value of the functional at the node when the node is a leaf and to the natural sum of the ranks of the immediate successors otherwise, and let zeta_s be the rank of the root (source lines 949-958).

Claim that zeta_{s+1} is strictly below zeta_s: the stage change opens one leaf nu of E[s], and by the twisting assumption every new descendant mu of nu has a strictly smaller functional value, so the natural sum of the corresponding powers of omega is strictly below the power at nu; propagate this up the ancestors to the root by induction along the finite chain (source lines 963-973).

Claim that zeta_s is below omega to the natural product of beta with omega for every stage, since the rank never increases and the rank at stage zero is already below omega raised to the natural product of beta with k (source line 975).

Conclude that the ranks give an M-infinite strictly decreasing sequence of ordinals below the bound, contradicting the well-foundedness hypothesis; hence the second case is impossible and the first case, which is the statement of the counted lemma, holds (source lines 977 and 1034).

proof_roadmap.step: Twist the functional, build the maximal universal enumeration and split into two cases.
Finite case: apply the finite-tree forcing lemma.
Infinite case: define the ordinal rank of a stage of the enumeration.
Prove the rank strictly decreases and stays below the bound.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:sem-wf-forcing-wf（源 932-934 行，证明 936-1034 行，其中活文到 977 行、其余为作者注释掉的长段）：SEM 力迫中任一条件都有扩展强制 Shore-blocking 泛函 Γ_k 称为部分函数。关键操作不是例行核验：先扭泛函使收敛单调且值严格下降（937-941 行），把它编码成 Σ⁰₁ 公式并取极大泛树枚举（944-945 行）；随后按树是否 M-有限分两类——有限类直接用有限树力迫引理（947 行），无限类则要给枚举的每个阶段定义**序数秩 ζ_s**（叶结点取 ω^{Γ 在叶处的值}、内结点取后继自然和，952-958 行），再证明 ζ_{s+1} < ζ_s（靠「阶段变化打开了某个叶、其所有后代的值都更小」逐层上推到根，963-973 行）同时 ζ_s 始终小于 ω^{β⨯ω}（975 行），从而得到与 WF(sup ω^{β⨯ω}) 矛盾的 M-无穷下降序列（977 行）。难点在于把「枚举在增长」翻译成序数严格下降，且两个 Claim 的界必须一致；原文位置在证明的 952-958、963-975 与 977 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Lemma lem:sem-wf-forcing-wf at source lines 932-934 together with the proof environment that begins two lines after the statement ends (936-1034); the pairing is the ordinary adjacent one. The live text of the proof ends at line 977 with the two claims; source lines 980-1033 are a commented-out earlier version of the same argument and are retained exactly as the author left them, because the closing \end{proof} at line 1034 belongs to this environment.

Six context spans are retained: the Shore-blocking lemma at 426-431, the definitions of nodes, trees, universality and satisfaction at 819-829 and 853-861, the statements of the two SEM tree lemmas at 863-865 and 893-897, and the definition of the forcing relation at 1121-1127. The retained preamble reproduces verbatim the author's document class at source line 2, his theorem declarations at source lines 16-25, his macro definitions at source lines 46-88 and 91, and his natural-operation macros at source lines 104-107, and it retains mathabx and cleveref; the stix-dependent LS2 block and the inputenc load with the utf8x option are not retained. mathabx supplies the natural sum symbol used in the rank definition.

No retained line contains a citation and the proof carries no bibliography, so the card needs none; the only cross-references of the proof are the author Cref calls to the three lemmas retained in the context.
